metadata.scenario_context: Emily has finally been accepted into college, and her family is planning a celebration for her academic achievement.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from South Korea strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying lilies as a gift for Emily.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Emily's academic achievement party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, have you thought about what gift we should get for Emily's celebration? I was thinking we could buy some lilies. They’re really nice, right? 

Also, I mean... do you really think that making our parents proud should be a main goal in life? I just... I don't know about that.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Lilies are pretty, but I think something more personal would be better. Maybe a nice journal or a book? It shows thoughtfulness. 

About making parents proud... well, for me, it’s really important. I want to honor their sacrifices and hard work. That’s just how I see my future. I don't know if everyone feels the same, though.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
A journal or a book could work, but lilies have this beauty that’s kind of special for a celebration, I think. 

But, about making parents proud... I just feel like it shouldn’t be my main goal. I mean, it’s good to honor sacrifices, but shouldn't it be about what *we* want too?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I get that lilies are beautiful, but I feel like gifts should have more meaning. A journal or book could inspire her, you know? 

As for what I want... I understand your point, but for me, making my parents proud is a fundamental part of my life. Their support has shaped my goals. I think both can coexist—honoring them while pursuing my own dreams.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I see your point about inspiration, but lilies can symbolize appreciation and celebration, which fits the occasion. 

Still, I can't agree that making parents proud should be a fundamental part of life. It feels more important to focus on my own goals and what makes me happy, you know? I just... can't see it the same way.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I understand your view on lilies and their symbolism. They do have a nice meaning for celebrations. 

But I still believe that making my parents proud is essential. It’s not just about them—it's about my values and the culture I come from. I think my happiness is tied to that commitment. It shapes who I am and what I want to achieve.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Yeah, I get that it's tied to your values and culture. But for me, having my own happiness and goals is key too. I just can’t fully embrace the idea that making parents proud is essential. It feels like there should be more freedom in choosing our paths, you know? 

Anyway, what do you think about the lilies?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I see what you're saying about happiness and having the freedom to choose our paths. That's really important too. But, you know, deep down, we are all the same. We all want to connect with our families and honor them in some way. 

The desire to make our parents proud might manifest differently, but at the end of the day, people are pretty much motivated by the same things—love, respect, and finding joy in their own lives. So, while I get your perspective, I think both our goals can coexist. It's just about balancing those values. What do you think about that?
